hints.content:
First, we note that $g(x)=f\left(\goldD{\dfrac13}x\right)$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

The expression $f(\goldD k\cdot x)$ when $|\goldD k|<1$ is a *horizontal stretch*: The $x$-value of every point on the graph of $y=f(x)$ is divided by $\goldD k$, so the points get further away from the $y$-axis.

Let's use this information to determine how the graph of $g$ should look.

The graph of $f$ passes through the points $(1,0)$ and $(3,1)$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So the graph of $g$ should pass through the following points:

- $\left(1\div\goldD{\dfrac13},0\right)=(3,0)$
- $\left(3\div\goldD{\dfrac13},1\right)=(9,1)$

options.alt: A log function graph labeled f on an x y coordinate plane. It passes through points (one, zero) and (three, one).
